topic: Effects of Heat on States of Matter
key_concepts: Heat is a form of energy called thermal energy, not matter
Heat flows from hot objects to cold objects
Temperature is measured using a thermometer
A rise in temperature causes atoms and molecules to move faster and farther apart
The three states of matter have different particle arrangements
Heating a solid can change it to a liquid, called melting
Cooling a liquid can change it back to a solid
Heating a liquid can change it to a gas, called evaporation
Condensation is the reverse process where a gas becomes liquid
Sublimation changes a solid directly to gas without becoming liquid
Freezing point is the temperature at which a liquid becomes solid
Water can change from solid to liquid to gas when heat is applied
